concentration.standard: U.S. DOJ/FTC Merger Guidelines (2023), Guideline 1: an HHI above 1,800 marks a highly concentrated market
concentration.method: HHI over the number of recorded ownership stakes (blocks) each holder has in the domain (not market share). Every open ownership stake is counted, at any percent, in blocks, HHI and reach; 'of which above 5%' shows how many were last reported above 5% (with no percent on record, a Form 3/4/5 ten-percent owner), so the split is visible and nothing is left out. Each measure is given twice: 'as filed' counts each filer separately; 'by family' adds a parent's units and duplicate records back to the parent (data/filer_families.json, each tie cited) and keeps a parent's stake its units now report separately (SEC Release No. 34-39538) as the parent's open stake, each holder-company pair once, so a parent whose units file separately is still seen as the parent (Josie 2026-10-14). The family HHI is the one that counts against the standard. A third figure, 'Schedule 13D/13G holders only', drops the Form 3/4/5 insiders (officers, directors and other ten-percent owners, each one block) and keeps the stakes reported on Schedule 13D/13G, by family: the concentration among institutional and activist holders alone (Josie 2026-10-24). Top-4 reach: share of the domain's mapped organizations the four most-connected holders sit in or own blocks of. Top-4 reach, 13D/13G holders only: of the domain's companies with at least one Schedule 13D/13G stake on record, the share held by the four families with the most such stakes (Josie 2026-10-24). A field with no ownership stake on record gets no concentration or reach figure. The last row adds every field together, each organization once: not a market under the standard, so the 1,800 line is not applied to it; shown for scale.
